title: The Last Summer
premise: Yara Coldharbour, a wedding planner who stopped believing in love after her own engagement collapsed, is hired to plan a wedding at Hollowmere Orchard — only to discover the deed lists two estranged co-owners: herself, via an inheritance she never claimed, and Theo Marchetti, the man who broke her heart a decade ago. The orchard's dying matriarch, Agnes, engineered the shared deed as a last test: the land can only be saved — and the wedding saved — if they learn to trust each other again before the harvest deadline and a predatory developer close in. As Yara and Theo restore the orchard and confront the old lie that separated them, they must choose between the safe, contained hearts they've built and the risk of loving wholly. In the end, they sign the deed together as partners in every sense, marry beneath the last blooming apple trees, and turn the orchard into a place where other broken people begin again.
about_author: Lior Zhou is the pen name of a former event planner who spent seven years orchestrating other people's happily-ever-afters before turning to fiction. They write love stories set in places where the past refuses to stay buried, and they still cry at real weddings — just quietly, from the back.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At a lavish wedding she's orchestrated to perfection, Yara watches the bride's smile flicker and feels nothing, reciting her private doctrine that the heart is a trainable muscle. A phone call summons her to Hollowmere Orchard for an urgent commission. Emotional beat: polished numbness beginning to crack.

chapters.title: A Letter in Green Ink
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The commission comes from Agnes Fairweather, the orchard's legendary elderly owner, whose letter is oddly personal — she knows Yara's history. The fee is triple market rate, with one condition: Yara must stay on-site until the wedding. Beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reviewing property documents at the farmhouse, Yara freezes: the deed names two co-owners — Agnes's trust, and herself, inherited through a grandmother she barely knew. The second name on the guest contract makes her drop her coffee: Theo Marchetti, best man. Beat: the past arriving without permission.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback, Yara's POV. Ten years ago, Yara and Theo were engaged; a single devastating letter ended it the week before the wedding. She remembers the accusation, his refusal to explain, and the ring left in a drawer. Beat: establishing the wound the whole story will probe.

chapters.title: The Man at the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Theo arrives to help prepare the orchard, and their first meeting is all barbed politeness and old electricity. He claims he didn't know she'd be here either — and shows her his copy of the same summons letter. Beat: suspicion that Agnes engineered everything.

chapters.title: Agnes's Terms
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Agnes, sharp and unapologetic, admits she brought them both here but reveals nothing of why, saying only: 'The orchard decides who stays.' She hands Yara the wedding file — the couple are Agnes's estranged grandchildren. Beat: the plot's chessboard revealed.

chapters.title: Bramble and Bone
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Walking the neglected orchard at dawn, Theo catalogues what's dying — trees, fences, something in himself. He took this job to face Yara at last, carrying a truth he's never told anyone. Beat: guilt and longing braided together.

chapters.title: The Guest List War
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Planning sessions with Theo turn into skirmishes over seating charts and symbolism, each choice a proxy battle for their history. When he defends her against a dismissive vendor, her armor dents. Beat: antagonism shading into reluctant respect.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A slick representative from Corvin Developments visits with a buyout offer that would save the orchard's debts — and raze it for a resort. Agnes refuses, but Yara learns the estate is drowning. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Cider at Midnight
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Caught by rain in the cider barn, Yara and Theo share the orchard's last bottle of homemade cider and, almost, a conversation about the past — until he flinches from the letter's subject. Beat: intimacy advancing, then retreating.

chapters.title: The Grandchildren Arrive
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Bride Priya and groom Callum arrive barely speaking, their wedding a family obligation neither seems to want. Yara recognizes the disease — love managed into silence — and sees her own reflection in it. Beat: the mirror couple established.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Agnes puts Theo to work grafting new trees onto old rootstock, lecturing that nothing grows from nothing cut clean. His hands remember this place; so does his grief for the father who once worked here. Beat: the orchard as metaphor taking root.

chapters.title: The Photograph in the Piano Bench
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Searching for wedding supplies, Yara finds a decades-old photograph: Agnes young, beside a man wearing Theo's face — his grandfather, and Agnes's own lost love. The parallels are too exact to be accident. Beat: the pattern of inherited heartbreak surfaces.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Yara and Theo alternating. A summer storm flattens the east rows; working through the night to save the trees, they move in wordless synchrony, and afterward, soaked and laughing, nearly kiss — interrupted by Priya, who watches with unreadable eyes. Beat: the almost.

chapters.title: Priya's Doubt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Priya privately asks Yara how you know when love is real, admitting she accepted Callum's proposal out of duty to Agnes. Yara, the professional skeptic, hears her own doctrine quoted back and hates how hollow it sounds. Beat: the theme turned inward.

chapters.title: The Letter, Part One
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered by a memory triggered in the farmhouse attic, Theo finally begins telling Yara about the letter he received ten years ago — from her grandmother, claiming Yara had asked him to end it. Yara goes white: she never wrote it. Beat: the central lie cracks open.

chapters.title: Forged
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Comparing the letter to her grandmother's surviving correspondence, Yara confirms the forgery — and realizes Agnes's green-ink summons matches the handwriting. Confronting Agnes yields only: 'I gave you both the truth. What you do with it is yours.' Beat: fury and vertigo.

chapters.title: Ten Lost Years
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Yara grieve the decade stolen from them — but grief curdles into blame. Why didn't he fight? Why didn't she call? Old wounds reopen as they realize the letter only worked because they were already afraid. Beat: the honest, painful reckoning.

chapters.title: The Harvest Deadline
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The accountant delivers the news: the orchard must turn a profit by harvest's end or the bank forces a sale to Corvin. The wedding is the last chance for revenue — and Agnes's health is visibly failing. Beat: stakes made concrete and urgent.

chapters.title: Working the Rows
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Montage of the orchard's revival: hired hands, farmers' market stalls, Yara's event skills turned to agritourism. Theo and Yara fall into partnership so seamless it frightens them both. Beat: love rebuilding through shared labor.

chapters.title: Callum's Secret
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo catches Callum on a late phone call, pleading and tender — with someone who is not Priya. Callum begs him to keep quiet, revealing he only proposed to honor a promise to Agnes. Beat: the mirror couple's fracture, echoing the theme of duty versus truth.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara, holding Callum's secret, agonizes: telling Priya betrays a client's trust; silence betrays the truth. She realizes she's spent ten years making the same choice — containment over honesty. Beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The rehearsal dinner Yara stages is flawless — until Agnes rises to toast and announces, to everyone's shock, that this wedding will happen in the orchard's oldest row, 'where love was lost, and where it will be found.' Yara understands: this wedding was always about them. Beat: Agnes's design fully revealed.

chapters.title: Kiss in the Old Row
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Under string lights in the oldest row, the tension breaks; Theo and Yara kiss, and it is ten years of grief and hunger at once. But afterward Yara pulls back: 'I don't lend pieces anymore. It's all or nothing.' Beat: the kiss, and the terms of the heart stated.

chapters.title: All or Nothing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara lays down her terms: she will not love halfway, not with secrets, not with exits. Theo, still hiding one final piece of his past — what really made him flee after the letter — cannot yet say yes. Beat: the central romantic obstacle sharpened.

chapters.title: The Thing He Never Told Her
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback: after the forged letter, Theo didn't just leave — he took a job that ruined his father's business and let Yara's family take the blame publicly, too ashamed to ever contest the story. His silence protected his pride, not her. Beat: his full culpability revealed.

chapters.title: Corvin Returns
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Corvin's representative makes a final, aggressive offer — and reveals they've been buying the debts of local suppliers, meaning the wedding itself may collapse. Agnes collapses the same night. Beat: external and internal crises converge.

chapters.title: The Hospital Vigil
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At Agnes's bedside, the estranged grandchildren, Theo, and Yara keep vigil. Agnes, lucid a final time, tells Yara: 'I forged one letter to undo another. Forgive me the method, not the mercy.' Beat: Agnes's motive humanized; forgiveness begun.

chapters.title: Priya Finds Out
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Priya discovers Callum's secret on her own, and the wedding teeters on cancellation. When Priya accuses Yara of knowing, Yara refuses to lie: 'I chose wrong. Don't repeat me.' Beat: Yara finally choosing truth over loyalty — her arc's turning point.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Almost Wasn't
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the wedding morning, Priya is gone. Yara, the planner who doesn't believe in weddings, tears up the script and tells Priya the truth about her own decade of containment: marriage isn't the risk; half-loving is. Beat: the mentor moment, doctrine overturned.

chapters.title: Vows in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Priya and Callum, stripped of pretense, choose each other honestly — or choose to part; they wed as truthful friends, vows rewritten in their own words. Watching them, Theo realizes he cannot ask Yara for 'all' while withholding his own worst truth. Beat: the mirror couple resolves; Theo resolves.

chapters.title: Confession at the Cider Press
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tells Yara everything — the forged letter, and the shame that kept him silent, the business, the blame. He offers no excuse, only the whole ugly truth and asks for nothing. Beat: the last secret surrendered; love made possible by truth.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Heart
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara walks the orchard all night with the deed in her hand. She can sign, sell her share to Corvin, and walk away safe and whole and contained — or stay and risk everything on a man and a place. Beat: the decision, held in suspension.

chapters.title: Signature in Green Ink
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At dawn, Yara signs the deed as co-owner — not for Theo, but for herself, claiming the inheritance and the life her grandmother's forgery stole twice over. Theo signs beside her. They are partners now, in land and in truth. Beat: climax of choice; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Corvin's Last Move
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Corvin files to contest the deed, but Agnes, from her hospital bed, springs her final trap: a conservation easement and a community fundraising drive Yara quietly seeded through her event network. The developer withdraws. Beat: external climax resolved by the couple's combined strengths.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The orchard's first harvest festival in years overflows with the whole cast: Priya and Callum, reconciled on honest terms; the townspeople; Agnes, home in a wheelchair, presiding. Yara watches the crowd she built and feels — unmistakably — belief. Beat: communal joy; the theme made visible.

chapters.title: The Proposal Under the Oldest Tree
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the oldest row, beneath the tree where Agnes and his grandfather once carved their initials, Theo proposes — no ring, just the deed amendment adding a line: 'and to Yara, everything, all of it.' She says yes before he finishes. Beat: the emotional climax; love against duty, won.

chapters.title: Agnes's Last Summer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Agnes dies at summer's end, in the farmhouse, at peace, leaving a final green-ink letter: 'I broke one love to test if it was real. It was. Forgive an old woman her science.' They bury her beneath the oldest tree. Beat: grief braided with gratitude; the architect's farewell.

chapters.title: The Wedding of Yara Coldharbour
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. One year later, Yara plans her own wedding — small, imperfect, honest — in the orchard she now co-tends. She walks the old row where everything was lost and found, and when she falters, the heart she trained so long to contain simply opens. Beat: full-circle resolution; belief earned.

chapters.title: Where Broken Things Grow
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, epilogue. The orchard becomes Hollowmere Trust, hosting weddings and retreats for people rebuilding after loss. Yara, planning a stranger's wedding, no longer recites the muscle theory — the heart, she writes in her new ledger, is not a muscle at all. It's an orchard: it grows back. Beat: thematic closure; the last line of the book.
